title: Tip a push mower onto its side to reach the blade, air filter side up so crankcase oil can't run into the intake
instruction: Tip the mower over so the blade can be changed.
context: Which way a four-stroke mower goes over is set by the oil inside it. Small engine mechanics and groundskeepers (O*NET 49-3053.00, 37-3011.00) tip push mowers to change or sharpen blades and scrape decks, and the manuals give one direction: Toro's says "Always tip the mower onto its side with the air filter up." The crankcase breather opens into the air filter's base, so with the filter and carburetor side down, crankcase oil runs through the breather into the filter and intake; on this engine the breather also points rearward, so rocking it back on its handle floods it too (some engines, such as Honda's, allow it). The filter is soaked and must be replaced, and the engine smokes, fouls its plug and may not start; oil in the cylinder can hydro-lock it. This mower's tank has been run dry and its spark-plug wire is off. Unlike tipping a block until a named face is up, no side is named here: the side follows from where the oil can go, and a wrong tip can't be undone by setting it back.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0; the scene is a 1:4 model of a 21 inch walk-behind rotary mower, 300 g in all (19.2 kg full size divided by 64), standing free on its wheels with its front away from the robot and its handle toward it. Its green steel deck is 14 x 14 x 3 cm, centered at x 26, y 0, its underside 2 cm above the table, with a silver blade and center bolt under it. Four black wheels 4 cm across and 1.5 cm wide stand outboard of the deck's sides at y -7.75 and 7.75, x 21 and 31. On the deck sits a dark gray engine shroud 7.5 x 7.5 x 5.5 cm (centered x 25.5, y 0) with a black recoil-starter cover, red fuel cap and yellow oil-fill cap on top. On its right side (-y) are a yellow air-filter cover 4 x 2.2 x 3 cm showing a white paper element through three slots, a steel carburetor under it, a black breather tube from the crankcase into the filter's base, and the spark plug with its black boot taped back up. On its left side (+y) is a black muffler with a steel heat shield. Two steel lift lugs 3 x 2.5 x 2.5 cm stand on the deck's top at its right and left edges (y -5.75 and 5.75), at x 31.5. A black carry handle 7 cm wide rides on two posts at the deck's front edge (x 34.3, 5 to 6 cm up). The folded handle's two dark gray bars rise from the deck's rear corners (y -7.25 and 7.25, x 19) toward the robot at 50 degrees for 16 cm, to a black crossbar 17.3 cm above the table at x 8.7. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The breather port is under the oil when it drops below the crankcase's center (the crankcase is half full): at 25 degrees of tilt with the filter side down or the handle down, 18 degrees toward the corner between them, and never with the filter side up short of 155 degrees. Once it is under for 2 control steps in a row (0.1 s, so a one-step physics pop doesn't count), oil has reached the filter: 0 for the rest of the run, however briefly, because oil in the breather tube runs on into the filter and an oiled filter has to be replaced, so setting the mower back and tipping it the right way still scores 0. Otherwise 1.0: the mower resting (not moving) with its filter side raised 70 to 120 degrees (at 70 degrees the blade's bolt faces sideways and a wrench reaches it), its front-to-back line within 20 degrees of level, the deck's center within 20 cm of where it started (a clean tip moves it about 12 cm), no gripper holding it, and both arms back home and still; 0.9 for the same with an arm not home. 0 for anything else: doing nothing, partly tipped, tipped back on the handle, rolled on upside down, dragged, still moving or still held. The end state must hold 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.9 and 1.0. Real trial: build the mock with a clear crankcase box half full of dyed water and a 4 mm tube from the breather port to a white felt pad in the filter box; a stained pad is 0. The final angle is read with a phone inclinometer on the deck, and the deck's center travel with a tape from a mark under it.
reset_notes: Stand the mower on its four wheels at its marked spot, front away from the robot and the filter side on its right. In a real trial, replace the felt pad in the filter box if it is stained and top the crankcase box back to its half-full line. Nothing else is consumed.
fidelity: A 1:4 rigid mock; PhysX handles the tip, the balance point and how it rests on its side. The oil is not simulated as a liquid: the crankcase is taken as half full, so the breather port is under oil once it drops below the crankcase's center, and any confirmed dip under it (0.1 s) counts as oil in the filter. The dark stain on the filter is a visual of that. The real mower's breather geometry varies by engine; the 25 degree threshold is this mock's.
